solution: Both groups have a central nervous system: in chordates it is dorsal, hollow and single, in non-chordates ventral, solid and double. A notochord is present only in chordates, a dorsal heart is absent only in chordates (they have a ventral heart), and a post-anal tail is absent only in non-chordates, so each of those belongs to one group alone. So the answer is option C.

NCERT: the proteins encoded by the genes cryIAc and cryIIAb control the cotton bollworms, and cryIAb controls the corn borer. Of the options, only Cry IAc acts on cotton bollworms; 'Cry II Ac' is not the gene NCERT names, and Cry IAb works on the corn borer. So the answer is option A.

In this method a single-stranded DNA or RNA probe, tagged with a radioactive molecule, is allowed to hybridise to its complementary DNA in a clone of cells, and the clone is then detected by autoradiography. NCERT: the clone having the mutated gene will not appear on the photographic film, because the probe has no complementarity with the mutated gene. So the answer is option D.

The DNA is first cut at specific locations by a restriction enzyme (B). The desired DNA fragment is then isolated (C) and its amount increased by PCR (D). Finally the recombinant DNA is introduced into the host cell (A). So the sequence is B, C, D, A. So the answer is option B.

In NCERT's map of the *E. coli* cloning vector pBR322, the BamHI site lies within the tetracycline resistance gene (A), the ampicillin resistance gene \(\text{amp}^R\) occupies the arc marked B, and the PstI site lies within the \(\text{amp}^R\) gene, next to the PvuI site (C). So the answer is option A.

NCERT: a unique vascular connection exists between the digestive tract and the liver, called the hepatic portal system. The hepatic portal vein carries blood from the intestine to the liver before it is delivered to the systemic circulation. So the answer is option D.

Both statements are true. NCERT: hormones that interact with membrane-bound receptors normally do not enter the target cell, but generate second messengers (such as cyclic AMP) which in turn regulate cellular metabolism. FSH, a protein hormone, acts this way. The Reason says how FSH brings about its effects from outside the cell; it does not say why FSH does not enter the cell, so it is not the explanation of the Assertion. So the answer is option B.

NCERT: sometimes the change in allele frequency is so different in the new sample of population that they become a different species. The original drifted population becomes the founders, and the effect is called the founder effect. So the answer is option C.

This number is not given in NCERT. In the usual textbook working, the glomerular blood (hydrostatic) pressure of about 70 mm Hg is opposed by the colloidal osmotic pressure of the plasma proteins (about 30 mm Hg) and the hydrostatic pressure of the fluid in Bowman's capsule (about 20 mm Hg). The net filtration pressure is \(70 - (30 + 20) = 20\) mm Hg. So the answer is option C.

The kangaroo rat of the North American deserts meets its water needs by the internal oxidation of fat, where water is a by-product (metabolic water, B), and it concentrates its urine so that very little water is used to remove wastes (highly hypertonic urine, C). It also cools and condenses the water in its exhaled air in the nasal passages (the nasal countercurrent mechanism, A). A protein-rich diet would produce more urea and need more water to remove it, so D does not help. So the answer is option A.

Angiotensin II raises blood volume in more than one way. It activates the adrenal cortex to release aldosterone, which causes the reabsorption of \(\text{Na}^+\) and water from the distal parts of the tubule (B). It also makes the proximal tubule reabsorb more NaCl and water (A), and it stimulates the release of ADH, which increases water reabsorption (C). So more than one of the options is correct. So the answer is option D.

NCERT: the central part of the thick (myosin) filament, not overlapped by the thin filaments, is called the H zone. It is not a gap between myosin filaments, so statement B is incorrect. Stimulation by a motor neuron at the neuromuscular junction, storage of minerals by the skeleton, and fibrous joints allowing no movement are all correct. So the answer is option B.

Amniocentesis can reveal the sex of the foetus and was misused for sex determination followed by MTP of a female foetus. To check female foeticide, NCERT lists a statutory ban on amniocentesis for sex determination among the steps taken. Legalising MTP and practising tubectomy do not address female foeticide. So the answer is option C.

NCERT: sterilisation is highly effective, but its reversibility is very poor, so it is the last option for most couples (i). It is also a surgical procedure (iii), it is held back by the misconception that it reduces sexual drive (ii), and facilities for it are lacking in many parts of the country (iv). All four reasons apply. So the answer is option D.

(i) is wrong: tubectomy blocks the fallopian tubes so that the egg cannot be carried to the uterus; it does not stop egg formation. (ii) is correct: the pills contain progestogens, or progestogen and estrogen together. (iii) is correct: the pills inhibit ovulation and implantation. (iv) is wrong: genital warts are caused by the human papillomavirus, not the herpes virus. (v) is correct: NCERT notes the rapid decline in the maternal mortality rate and the infant mortality rate. So (ii), (iii) and (v); option D names a statement (vi) that the question does not have. So the answer is option B.

In in vitro fertilisation, the ova and sperms are fused in the laboratory to form a zygote. NCERT: the zygote or early embryos, with up to 8 blastomeres, are transferred into the fallopian tube (ZIFT), and embryos with more than 8 blastomeres into the uterus (IUT). An ovum is transferred into the fallopian tube only in GIFT. So the answer is option B.

Statement B is incorrect. NCERT: lactational amenorrhea is effective only up to a maximum of six months after parturition, while the mother breastfeeds fully; it has a time limit. Periodic abstinence avoids coitus from day 10 to 17 of the cycle, withdrawal prevents sperm from entering the vagina, and natural methods have almost no side effects but a high chance of failure, so A, C and D are correct. So the answer is option B.

NCERT: sexually transmitted infections spread by sexual contact, and some of them, such as hepatitis-B and HIV, also by sharing injection needles or surgical instruments with infected persons, by transfusion of blood, or from an infected mother to the foetus. So (b) and (c) are correct. Sterile needles do not spread infection, and kissing and inheritance are not ways these diseases spread. So the answer is option D.

Statement B is incorrect. In the cockroach the ring of 6 to 8 blind tubules called gastric (hepatic) caecae is present at the junction of the foregut and the midgut, not the midgut and the hindgut. The 10th abdominal segment bears a pair of anal cerci in both sexes, the hypopharynx lies within the cavity enclosed by the mouth parts, and in females the 7th to 9th sterna together form a genital pouch. So the answer is option B.

In the figure of each option, labels above an arrow leaving the tubule are reabsorbed into the blood, and labels below an arrow entering the tubule are secreted into the filtrate. NCERT: the proximal tubule (P) reabsorbs \(\text{HCO}_3^-\), NaCl and water and secretes \(\text{H}^+\) and ammonia; the distal tubule (D) reabsorbs NaCl, water and \(\text{HCO}_3^-\) and secretes \(\text{H}^+\) and \(\text{K}^+\). Only diagram (2) shows this. Diagram (1) shows water secreted in the proximal tubule, diagram (3) shows NaCl secreted in the distal tubule, and diagram (4) shows water secreted and ammonia reabsorbed. So the answer is option B.

Compound eyes are made of ommatidia, so B is the correct match.
Alary muscles are associated with the heart of the cockroach, not with its nervous system (A).
The fat body is not a digestive gland (C).
The hypopharynx is not a grinding region (D).
So the answer is (B) Compound eyes and Ommatidia.

NCERT: relaxin is secreted by the ovary in the later phase of pregnancy; in the ovary it comes from the corpus luteum.
The uterus, the Graafian follicle and the foetus do not secrete relaxin in the later phase of pregnancy.
So the answer is (C) Corpus luteum.

The figure shows the pBR322 map with \(\text{amp}^R\) and \(\text{tet}^R\) genes, the ori site and the rop gene.
\(\text{Amp}^R\) and \(\text{tet}^R\) are antibiotic resistance genes, so option D is correct.
Ori is the origin of replication, not a restriction enzyme.
rop is not about osmotic pressure; it codes for the proteins involved in the replication of the plasmid. Ori is the sequence that controls the copy number of the linked DNA.
Eco RI and Hind III are restriction sites, not selectable markers.
So the answer is (D) \(\text{Amp}^R\), \(\text{tet}^R\) antibiotic resistance genes.

Homo habilis, Australopithecines and Ramapithecus all lived millions of years ago, before the lineage that led to modern man.
Homo erectus lived later, about 1.5 million years ago, by NCERT's date, so it is the most recent of the four.
So the answer is (D) Homo erectus.
